summary: Space-yard is a narrative-driven 3D exploration game built in Godot that brings inactive space equipment: like the Mars Opportunity rover, back to life. By presenting authentic NASA mission logs in a more entertaining and gamified way, we allow players to experience the harsh realities of planetary exploration firsthand. It is an interactive story about hardship, resilience, and transience. We believe it is crucial to honor the forgotten mechanical heroes of our space programs in an entertaining medium, transforming real scientific data into an emotional journey that educates and inspires younger audiences to care about space history.
details:
How It Works & What It Does
 Space Yard is a short narrative game that lets players drive NASA’s Opportunity rover across Meridiani Planum and relive key moments of its mission. Guided by voiced transmissions from JPL Control, players follow glowing waypoints, analyze rocks for hematite “blueberries,” and descend into a crater whose layered bedrock points to ancient liquid water. A live telemetry HUD tracks power, solar input, and the data link. When the primary science goals are done, a planet-wide dust storm rolls in: fog and darkness rise, solar power collapses, the rover locks down, and the story ends the way the real mission did - with silence.

Creative Approach & Decision Making
 We focused on Opportunity because its story - built for 90 days, lasting 15 years - is one of the most human in space exploration. Early on we considered a set of small 2D minigames about different instruments. We chose instead one detailed 3D experience: immersion and emotional payoff mattered more than breadth. While other games explore the Moon or Mars, few tell the story of a retired spacecraft that people grew up following. We designed the mission around real milestones (landing, geology, water evidence, the final storm) and kept controls simple so the narrative could lead.

Technology Stack
 The project was built in Godot 4.7 with GDScript. We used an official NASA 3D MER model with working rocker-bogie suspension, procedural Martian terrain streamed in chunks, and a mission system that paces dialogue, waypoints, sample analysis, and the storm finale. Voice lines were generated with ElevenLabs; the music was composed by a team member in Bosca Ceoli.

Impact & Benefits
 We want the game to spark curiosity about space exploration in younger players, and nostalgia in people who followed Opportunity in real time. An interactive story can make planetary science feel personal: you don’t just hear that Oppy found water - you drive there and sample it. Longer term, we see Space Yard as the first chapter in a series about the forgotten mechanical heroes of space.
